2. The question arises from an order of the High Court of Bangladesh, passed on appeal from an order of rejection of obligation filed by the judgment-debtor-appellant under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Respondent upon a dispute arising from a contract to supply 1500 bales of jute obtained an award from the tribunal of Arbitration of the Narayanganj Chamber of Commerce and Industries, to receive a sum of 2,06,250/-. The award, after being confirmed by the Civil Court, was put into execution and the appellant find objection under section 47 of the Civil Procedure Code, which was rejected by the executing court by an order dated 27.12.69. From this order judgment-debtor filed an appeal being F.M.A. no. 90 of 1970, before the Dacca High Court. During the pendency of this appeal on 6th of October, 1971, the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal that was taken from the award before that court. The High Court of Bangladesh on 3rd of July, 1972 dismissed the appeal taken from the execution proceeding by the appellant holding that the question whether the decree holder is a firm or a person could not be agitated in the execution proceeding, as the executing court cannot go behind the decree. It was urged before the High Court that the judgment of the Supreme Court delivered on 6th October, 1971 was not a valid judgment, and the appeal before the Pakistan Supreme Court should be treated as transferred to and pending before the Appellate Division, and the appeal before the High Court be decided only after the decision given by the Appellate Division. The High Court, of course, gave no opinion on this question, and made its observation on the legal personality of the decree holder and dismissed the appeal. Now if the judgment of the Supreme Court is not a valid judgment, then this court is to treat that appeal as pending before this court and pronounce its own judgment upon it, and then the fact of the present appeal will depend upon that decision. But if the judgment of the Supreme Court is a valid judgment, then there is no merit in this appeal. 

 6. Chronologically, next, came the High Court of Bangladesh Order, 1972 (President's Order 5 of 1972), on 17th January, 1972. This Order relates to the jurisdiction and power of the High Court of Bangladesh, and the position of the Dacca High Court between 26th day of March, 1971 till the coming into existence of the High Court of Bangladesh, but is silent about the Supreme Court. Then came Bangladesh (Legal Proceedings) Second Order 1972 (P.O. 69 of 1972), published in Dacca Gazette, on 16th June, 1972. A significant provision is contained in article 5(1) of this Order. It says that subject to clause (2), any Judgment, decree, order,  award or decision passed made or given by the Supreme Court of Pakistan, or by any court or by any tribunal, arbitrator, tax authority or other authority, in Bangladesh, in any legal proceedings by or against the erstwhile Government of Pakistan or Government of East Pakistan arising out of the matters within the territories of Bangladesh shall be enforceable. 

 7. In this Order, for the first time, we get a reference to the judgment passed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan, and the Order relates to the liability of Bangladesh Government, arising from a judicial or quasi-judicial decision and it clearly and manifestly says that the judgment and decree of the Supreme Court of Pakistan shall be enforceable. This is subject to the discretion of Bangladesh Government to pray for abatement of the proceeding before the appropriate Tribunal, if it desire when the legislative authority has clearly expressed its mind on 16th day of June 1972, as to the operative power of a decision of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, no further speculation of any supposed intention in the Proclamation of Independence, is to be searched for.
